What exists now: \\u0060IMessageTransport.SquashAsync\\u0060 carries a \\u0060lowWaterMark\\u0060 parameter; both \\u0060GitLedgerMessageTransport\\u0060 and \\u0060InMemoryMessageTransport\\u0060 write and read it back inside \\u0060ReadSinceAsync\\u0060, resuming a cold or stale reader at the mark instead of stalling on the pruned range below it. \\u0060MessageOutbox.SquashAsync\\u0060 computes the mark from \\u0060survivors\\u0060/\\u0060sent\\u0060 (both already ordered ascending by seq). Two tests in \\u0060MessageTransportTests.cs\\u0060 cover it: the restored cold-read test and a new one proving a real gap above the mark still stalls.\\n- Gotcha: the mark lives at a fixed path (\\u0060low-water-mark\\u0060) outside \\u0060messages/\\u0060 in the git-backed transport, deliberately so \\u0060ls-tree ... -- messages/\\u0060 never picks it up as a candidate envelope; if anyone ever widens that pathspec, this needs re-checking. The mark is monotonically non-decreasing across squashes purely because retention cutoff only ever increases, not because anything enforces it directly, so any future change to how survivors are computed should preserve that property or the resume logic can regress.\\n- Left undone: no CLI or \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 surface for the mark itself, since nothing outside the transport\\u0027s own gap-stop decision needs to see it today.
